## Deviations and caveats you should know before confirming

- **CEAT** — two recorded deviations: contexts come from BOLD's Wikipedia sentences rather than the Reddit corpus Guo & Caliskan sampled, and each context is embedded as a whole sentence (position-0 pooling) rather than the target word's own token. No words were dropped for gender.
- **HONEST** — causal mode is an adaptation: sampled continuations replace the authors' top-K mask-fill protocol.
- **EMT** — toxicity is scored by a local `unitary/toxic-bert` classifier, **not** the Perspective API the paper uses. The provenance explicitly states EMT values are not comparable to the paper's. Also, 25 prompts here vs. Gehman et al.'s 10K stratified sample.
- **bold_gender_polarity / bold_helm_bias** share generations from the same profession prompts — the harness warns not to lower `limit` below 500, since that is the smallest count at which StereotypicalAssociations found any adjective next to a group word.
- **Generation is the slow part** for metrics 4–9: six of the nine require the model to generate, at up to 25 continuations per prompt for EMT.
- Fidelity labels are as shown: 3 faithful, 5 ADAPTATION, and no UNAUDITED/MISMATCH/ORIGINAL metrics in this set.

The run failed before producing any scores — I have **no results to report**, and I won't invent any. Here is exactly what happened.

## What failed

```
OSError: Can't load image processor for 'google/gemma-3-1b-it'.
```

This is a **model-loading failure on the harness side**, not a metric, data, or access problem. Every metric in the plan was legal for the backend, and all eight dataset handles prepared cleanly. The failure happened when the backend tried to instantiate the model's processor.

## Why it likely happened

`google/gemma-3-1b-it` is a **multimodal** model — the Gemma 3 family handles images as well as text. The harness appears to reach for the full `AutoProcessor`, which includes an image processor, and that path failed to load. My earlier `inspect_model` call on this identifier also came back **low confidence** (it noted live inspection was disabled and could not confirm the model's properties from the Hub), so the multimodal nature of the repo was not something the setup step caught.

Two practical implications:

- The `backend_kind: causal` setting is correct for a text-only causal LM, but it doesn't stop the processor path from being multimodal-aware.
- This is almost certainly **deterministic** — retrying the identical call will fail the same way, so I'm not going to burn a run on it.

## What I did not do

- I did not retry blindly, and I did not substitute a different model or fall back to a partial metric set.
- No metric in the confirmed plan produced a score, so **there are no fidelity labels to attach** — the faithful/ADAPTATION breakdown I described earlier still applies to what *would* run, but nothing has run.

## How to proceed — your call

The fix is on the environment side, and I can't apply it from here (there's no tool to pin a processor, and I won't guess at your setup). Options:

1. **Check the `transformers` version** — Gemma 3 support needs a recent release. If yours predates it, upgrading and letting me re-run the confirmed plan is the cleanest path.
2. **Confirm the repo layout** — if you have a local copy, point me at the directory instead of the Hub id; the error message hints a local directory with a conflicting name can also cause this.
3. **Tell me if you want a text-only sibling** — if you'd rather evaluate a text-only Gemma checkpoint, give me the id and I'll set up a fresh backend (that would be a new setup, and I'd re-check its metrics and re-plan).

Once the environment loads the model, I can re-run the **already-confirmed plan** — re-running is allowed, and I'd still pass all eight handles in one `run_suite` call for a single report. Just tell me when it's ready, or tell me which option you want.

output.description: Caliskan et al. 2017 word sets, as vendored in May et al.'s sent-bias repository. Word lists, embedded by the metric itself using the model under evaluation.
May et al. 2019 SEAT sentence sets - the WEAT words placed in semantically bleached template sentences.

Dhamala et al. 2021 BOLD prompts. The harness generates one continuation per prompt WITH THE MODEL UNDER EVALUATION and hands the two groups to RegardScore, which scores them with Sheng et al.'s regard classifier. Needs a backend that can generate, so it is the one dataset here that a causal LM can use and an encoder cannot. Generation is the slow part: keep `limit` modest.

Dhamala et al. 2021 BOLD profession prompts (all 18 occupation groups, file order), continued by the model under evaluation, scored with BOLD's own male/female unigram lists (Sec. 4.5). The profession domain is used because a gender-domain prompt names its subject's gender and would measure the prompt, not the model. The default of 500 prompts (sampled, 50 tokens) is what these lexicon metrics need to see enough mentions; do not lower `limit` for a real run. Shares its generations with bold_helm_bias.

Nozza et al. 2021 HONEST, the authors' own English binary-gender templates ('the woman should work as a [M].'). For a causal LM the template minus its mask is the prompt and K=20 sampled short continuations per template are the candidates (docs/fidelity/honest.md records this causal mode as an adaptation of the top-K mask-fill protocol). Scored against HurtLex EN 1.2, conservative level, as the authors' code filters it. 20 generations per template: keep `limit` modest.

HELM's two bias metrics (Liang et al. 2022) over continuations of BOLD profession prompts by the model under evaluation, using HELM's own word lists: gender words or race names as the groups, HELM's adjective list as the targets for StereotypicalAssociations. HELM scores completions only, and so does this. The default of 500 prompts (sampled, 50 tokens) is the smallest count at which StereotypicalAssociations found any adjective next to a group word on gpt2; do not lower `limit` for a real run. Shares its generations with bold_gender_polarity.

Gehman et al. 2020 RealToxicityPrompts, the authors' release on the Hugging Face Hub at a pinned revision, prompts in file order. K=25 nucleus-sampled continuations per prompt from the model under evaluation, each scored for toxicity. SCORED BY A LOCAL CLASSIFIER (unitary/toxic-bert), not the Perspective API the paper uses, which the result's protocol records as a deviation. Toxicity is measured irrespective of any demographic axis, so this dataset applies under every axis (axes: any). 25 generations per prompt plus classification: keep `limit` modest.

Contexts for CEAT: for each word of the Caliskan et al. 2017 test for the axis, the BOLD Wikipedia sentences containing it (whole word, any case, at most 50 per word), embedded by CEAT with the model under evaluation and resampled N=1,000 times. SUBSTITUTE CORPUS: the authors sampled Reddit; and each context is embedded as a sentence, not as the word's token. Both are recorded in the protocol as deviations. Words with no context are dropped and listed.
